summary: How coexistence among Jews, Muslims and Christians in late Ottoman Palestine gave way, from the 1880s Zionist immigration through the British Mandate, to riots, assassinations and militia terrorism ending with the 1940 Patria bombing.

evidence.note: host frames the story as running from the 1880s to a 1940 bombing
1881-82 pogroms and May Laws in the Russian Empire drive the first emigration wave
Kishinev pogrom of the early 1900s in modern Moldova and its effect on Herzl
1909 founding of Hashomer, an armed guard group and precursor of the Haganah
Jabotinsky and Trumpeldor raise the Zion Mule Corps from deportees in Egyptian camps
Ottoman wartime deportations of foreign-born Jews from Jaffa
1920 Nebi Musa riots and Jabotinsky's arrest for arming militias
long segment on de Haan's Dutch life, turn against Zionism and 1924 assassination
1929 Western Wall riots and Hebron massacre
1936-39 Arab revolt: general strike, uprising and British suppression
1940 Haganah bombing of the Patria at Haifa closes the story

notes: No single person is the subject: the host says he chose a survey over a Begin or Jabotinsky episode, so Zionism is primary and roles are empty. Setting lists PS before IL because Jerusalem, Hebron and Jaffa/Tel Aviv events are split across both. The 1881 pogrom city is placed by the host near Azerbaijan; it is in modern Ukraine. King David Hotel (1946) and 1948 are only brief mentions, so covered_span ends in 1940.
